8207.name: Store Room

up.description: To the up lies Modest Farmhouse And Barn.

8207.description:
Sacks of meal, a rack of hams and a stack of empty barrels crowd this
low cellar room beneath the farmhouse. The walls are plain planking over
packed earth, and the air smells of dust, apples and old sacking. Behind
the barrels the boards sound oddly hollow when you knock them, as if a
false wall hid something better kept out of sight. A ladder climbs up
through the trapdoor to the house above.

8219.name: The Top Of The Stairs

north.description: To the north lies Zert's Room.

east.description: To the east lies A Private Room.

south.description: To the south lies Gundigoot's Quarters.

west.description: To the west lies Furnok's Room.

down.description: To the down lies The Inn Of The Welcome Wench.

8219.description:
A narrow landing at the head of the inn stair, its floorboards worn pale
down the middle by travellers' boots. Four stout doors face one another
across the little space: a door ahead of you, one to your left, one to
your right and one behind you, each with a heavy iron lock. A single
candle sputters in a wall sconce, and the smell of bread and ale rises
faintly from the common room as the stair winds down toward it.
Somewhere beyond a door, a floorboard creaks.

8220.name: The Secret Store Room

south.description: To the south lies The Store Room.

up.description: To the up lies The Inn Of The Welcome Wench.

8220.description:
This hidden chamber lies behind a wall that looks solid from the other
side, and it is far too tidy for a mere pantry. Iron-bound chests stand
in a row against the stone, each with a lock of better quality than any
innkeeper would buy. Dust lies thin on the floor, and a faint oily smell
hangs in the air. A narrow way leads on to the larger store room, and a
stair climbs up to the inn above.

8221.name: Gundigoot's Quarters

north.description: To the north lies The Top Of The Stairs.

down.description: To the down lies The Kitchen Of The Welcome Wench.

8221.description:
Gundigoot lodges well, for a man who claims to be a simple traveller:
the bed is hung with a heavy green curtain, a brass lamp stands on a
polished table, and a good carpet hides the boards. A locked coffer sits
at the foot of the bed, and a plain cloak hangs on a peg beside the door
to the landing. A narrow back stair spirals down toward the warm
kitchen, where the heat of the hearth seeps up through the floor.

8222.name: The Store Room

north.description: To the north lies The Secret Store Room.

up.description: To the up lies The Kitchen Of The Welcome Wench.

8222.description:
Barrels of ale, kegs of salted pork and crates of crockery fill this
long store room beneath the inn, stacked high and hung with cobwebs. A
single oil lamp in a niche throws shadows over the beams, and the floor
is damp where the casks sweat. One wall is oddly thicker than the rest,
with a seam running down it that looks too straight for age. A stair
rises up to the kitchen, and a narrow way leads toward a hidden chamber.

8223.name: Zert's Room

south.description: To the south lies The Top Of The Stairs.

8223.description:
This is a cramped, tidy chamber with a narrow bed, a travelling chest
bound in iron and a stool beside a shuttered window. The coverlet is
pulled so tight it might have been ironed, and the whitewashed walls
bear not one picture. Look closely at the beam above the bed, though,
and you will find a small eye cut into the wood, half hidden by a smear
of soot. The only way out is the door back to the landing.

extra_descs.eye beam:
An eye no bigger than your thumb is carved into the beam, its pupil
blackened with soot. It is cut so neatly that it could only be the work
of a patient hand, and it faces the bed.

8224.name: A Private Room

west.description: To the west lies The Top Of The Stairs.

8224.description:
The room is comfortable enough for a well-paying guest, with a wide bed,
a washstand and a rag rug before a small hearth that has not been lit in
days. A cheerful sampler about hospitality hangs by the window. The
bedding is rumpled, a half-burned candle stands in a puddle of wax on
the sill, and the air smells faintly of stale smoke. The door to the
landing stands to your left.

8225.name: Furnok's Room

east.description: To the east lies The Top Of The Stairs.

8225.description:
Furnok keeps a barer room than his companions: a pallet, a bench and a
basin, and the shutters nailed fast against the village outside.
Scratches in the plaster by the bedhead form a pattern of crossed lines
that is not quite a letter and not quite a pictogram. A stub of tallow
burns on the floor, and the air is close and sour. The only door leads
out to the landing.

8241.name: The Upper Hall

east.description: To the east lies The Assistant Cleric's Quarters.

west.description: To the west lies The Chief Priest's Chambers.

up.description: To the up lies The Upper Hall.

down.description: To the down lies The Vestry.

8241.description:
The upper hall of the church is long and silent, lit by narrow windows
glazed in thick, greenish glass. Oak beams curve overhead, and the
floorboards are polished by the soft shoes of priests. Doors stand at
either end, one to the quarters of the priest's assistant and the other
to the chief priest's chambers, each with an iron latch. A plain stair
leads down to the vestry, and a lingering smell of beeswax and incense
hangs in the air.

8242.name: The Sacred Trophies Gallery

up.description: To the up lies The Study And Audience Chamber.

8242.description:
The Sacred Trophies Gallery is a long, dim loft under the church roof,
where glass-fronted cases line the walls and the rafters hang with faded
banners. Chalices, reliquaries and crumbling scrolls of old victories
lie on velvet, each tagged in a careful hand. The floor creaks softly
underfoot, and the light is dusty and amber. A steep stair climbs up to
the study and audience chamber.

8243.name: The Assistant Cleric's Quarters

west.description: To the west lies The Upper Hall.

8243.description:
A small, ordered chamber, with a narrow bed, a writing desk under the
window and a shelf of well-thumbed prayer books. The assistant cleric
keeps his things neat, and a simple wooden symbol of Helver hangs above
the pillow. The room smells of ink and lamp oil. Something about the
ceiling is wrong, though, for a faint pattern of scratches has been cut
into the corner plaster, as if someone had drawn the same small mark
over and over. The door leads back to the hall.

8244.name: The Chief Priest's Chambers

east.description: To the east lies The Upper Hall.

8244.description:
Rich hangings of crimson and gold cover the walls of this chamber, and a
great bed stands on a low dais beneath a canopy of embroidered silk. A
heavy desk, a carved prayer stool and a silver lamp suggest comfort far
beyond a village priest's means. The shutters are closed tight, and the
air is warm and a little too sweet. Behind the hangings you glimpse the
edge of a hidden recess, and the door out to the hall stands at your
back.
